title: Cauchy integral and derivative formulas
section: Complex Variables ▷ Theorems Concerning Analytic Functions
terms: Cauchy integral formula; Cauchy derivative formula; simple closed contour; positive orientation.

exposition.text:
If f is holomorphic on an open neighborhood of a simple closed contour and its interior, and a
R
n+1 (n)
is inside, then for positive orientation f(z)/(z − a) dz = 2πif (a)/n!, for n ≥ 0. The n = 0
C
case is Cauchy’s integral formula.
Identify the analytic numerator and the denominator power before differentiating: a power
n + 1 requires the nth derivative. If a is outside the contour and no other singularities occur,
the integral is zero. Clockwise orientation changes the sign, and a singularity on the contour
invalidates the ordinary formula.
A simple closed contour is a closed curve with no self-intersections apart from the identified
starting and ending point. Positive orientation is counterclockwise around its interior (the in-
terior stays on the left as the curve is followed). These hypotheses give one positive winding
around each interior point in the stated formula.
